text.p: SKOPJE, March 25 - These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana, on his first visit to Macedonia, says he is impressed with Macedonia's progress in catching up with Partnership for Peace programme.
- Macedonian Government to hold vote of confidence in government at request of Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski.

- Crvenkovski announced a decisive battle against organized crime connected with the TAT scandal; opposition IMRO-DPMNY postponed its protest planned for March 27 to give minister time to make good on his promises.
- Trial of TAT owner Sonja Nikolovska and three of her employees expected in mid-April.
- Macedonia to send 2,000 tonnes of flour to Bulgaria and humanitarian aid.

- Partnership for peace military exercise code-named Saviour to be held at Krivolak range May 11 through 17. Units from Macedonia, U.S., Italy, Turkey, Greece, Bulgaria, Romani, Slovenia and Albania will take part.
